title: Sacred Pool
html:
The Sacred Pool is a Location within the Emerald Grove in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3.
“
Do you hear them? The birds. They're beautiful. I've thought of nothing but goblins and tieflings for so long, I stopped listening.
„
— Elwyn, after the grove has its problems solved

Overview

The Sacred Pool is the central part of the Emerald Grove. It connects to the Hollow, the Secluded Cove and the Inner Sanctum. It also has direct access to the grove ramparts.

The Sacred pool is located in the basin's lowest point, with a path running down to the river shore, and another one, ascending to the cliffs of the Secluded Cove. In the centre of it is a cromlech where a druidic ritual, the Rite of Thorns, is being processed with the  Idol of Silvanus as its focus placed atop the centre stone.

Access

The main entry to the Sacred Pool is accessed by descending the staircase from The Hollow at X: 251 Y: 547. An alternate entry is through the elevator in the southern ramparts of the Emerald Grove at X: 242 Y: 480. However, this path is initially blocked by a sleeping bear.

Alternatively, it is possible to descend into the basin from a cliff approximately at X: 210 Y: 490 using means of spatial movement like  Feather Fall,  Misty Step or  Grant Flight.

Upon approaching the main entry for the first time, the party can see  Jeorna,  Maggran and  Mino barring the tieflings from entering the Sacred Pool. In a show of force to ward them off, Maggran shapeshifts himself into a bear. After the tieflings are turned away from the entrance, the party can interact with  Locke and  Komira, to find out that the druids intend to (summarily) judge one of tiefling children,  Arabella, for her attempt to steal the  Idol of Silvanus; this initiates the quest ⁠Save Arabella.

Afterwards, the party can also speak to the trio of druid guards, who move to stop the party as well, but eventually relent, stating that the new First Druid  Kagha wishes to speak with them.

Points of interest

Central basin

In the centre Sacred Pool, five druids stand around the cromlech:  Aelar,  Elwyn,  Inwe,  Karrik and  Tahan. They perform the Rite of Thorns using the Idol of Silvanus in the middle. The idol can be stolen by the party on  Mol's request throughout the ⁠Steal the Sacred Idol quest. Successful theft grants the following inspiration:

  • ⁠Heretic inspiration for characters with the  Criminal background
  • ⁠Idolatry inspiration for characters with the  Urchin background
  • ⁠Treefather's Sorrow inspiration for characters with the  Acolyte background - only along with killing the grove druids[verify].

To the north, a man in colourful clothes by the name of  Volo interviews the bear  Bosk. If a party member speaks with Volo, he asks them to describe the recent goblin attack to him. However, it becomes clear soon enough that the report Volo is writing has nothing common with their words or the real events. If the player character speaks to Bosk via  Speak with Animals, he seems to be disappointed with the results of the interview as well. Volo then declares his intent to personally investigate the new Cult of the Absolute spreading among the goblins, and journeys to the Goblin Camp after a long rest.

Telling a glamourized story to Volo grants the ⁠A Very Tall Tale inspiration to characters with the  Entertainer background. Volo can also act as a trader, but his wares can only be accessed at this time using the 'Trade' option in the lower-left corner within the dialogue cutscene.

Cliff overlook

A path starting from the Sacred pool basin at X: 275 Y: 523 forms a T-junction leading up and south and straight to north-west. The southern path eventually comes to an overlook where  Alfira, a tiefling bard apprentice is struggling to create a new song in memory of the recent tragic death of her mentor Lihala. Two squirrels,  Corinna and  Spar, are painfully listening to her attempts. The player character can choose to discourage Alfira or help her. Helping her finish the song results in a beautiful cutscene where Alifra sings the the song while playing on her lute. This earns the ⁠A Bard's Muse inspiration for characters with the  Entertainer background.

Behind a stone column at X: 292 Y: 483 a locked gilded chest is hidden and requires a  DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check to be lockpicked. It contains the  Cap of Curing, and looting it is not considered a crime.

The beginning of the path is one of the possible locations where  Raphael may be encountered for the first time in the walkthrough.

The north-western path from the T-junction leads to the Secluded Cove location.

River shore

At the eastmost corner of the Sacred Pool, a sandy path runs down to the river shore. The bear Ormn is catching fish on a small beach. An  Amulet of Silvanus is hidden beneath a movable flat rock in this area at X: 262 Y: 481. Also, a series of jumps onto rocks beyond Ormn allows to reach a wooden chest at X: 288 Y: 449 containing gold and random alchemical ingredients.

Elevator to the ramparts

To the south from the cromlech is a wooden elevator, which leads up to the ramparts. However, the movable platform is blocked by the slumbering bear  Tuffet. To make her move aside, any party member can interact with her: pass a  DC 10 Animal Handling Check, politely ask her via  Speak with Animals, or throw a fish near the elevator.[1] Lured by the scent, Tuffet moves from the platform and falls asleep again nearby; afterwards, the elevator can be freely used in both directions.

To the west of the elevator a blue jay named  Topaz tries to decorate his nest with several metallic trinkets; among these are a gold coin and a  Shiny Key. Convincing him via  Speak with Animals that the pieces of metal are inappropriate makes the jay throw them out of nest, then safe to pick up.[2] The key opens the shiny chest atop a stone pillar to the north-west, at X: 222 Y: 497.

Using the  Deception dialogue option when speaking with Topaz to make him dispose of the coin and the key is considered an oathbreaking action for  Paladins of the Crown.

Inner Sanctum entrance

At X: 228 Y: 510 the druid  Apikusis tends to a small patch of herbs and flowers, where some alchemical ingredients can be cropped. Upon first approaching her, she is talking to the blue jay  Tingmiaq, sending her to search for 'master'. If spoken to, Apikusis turns out to be one of the few grove druids who do not agree with  Kagha's attitude towards the refugees. However, she is aware of being outvoted and does what she can to return back the real leader of the grove,  Halsin.

The bird Tingmiaq can be spoken to via  Speak with Animals before he departs. He can tell the party of some kinds of danger surrounding the grove.

The carved stone door at X: 223 Y: 525 leads to the cavernous part of the sacred ground, the Inner Sanctum.[3] There the party can progress or resolve several quests like ⁠Find a Cure, ⁠Save Arabella, ⁠Save the Refugees, as well as some others.

Notes and references

  1. ↑ This is possible if the party read a note from Halsin to Nettie, where he asks not to overfeed Tuffet. The party member must choose a respective option within the dialogue with Tuffet; tossing camp supplies outside of the dialogue does nothing. Fresh fish can be found near Ormn's beach.
  2. ↑ The dialogue with Topaz is built around the coin only, but if successful he eventually disposes of both items. There is also an option to shoo the bird away, which has the same result, but both coin and key remain red-outlined, and taking them is still considered a theft.
  3. ↑ There is no such location on the in-game map. The area beyond the stone door is marked as Emerald Grove. "Inner Sanctum" is a term used by the wiki to help disambiguate.
